chunks.arabic_text: الكَافِي: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى وَالْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ جَمِيعًا، عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa and al-Hasan ibn Mahbub together, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ اخْتَلَفَ عَلَيْهِ رَجُلَانِ مِنْ أَهْلِ دِينِهِ فِي أَمْرٍ كِلَاهُمَا يَرْوِيهِ: أَحَدُهُمَا يَأْمُرُ بِأَخْذِهِ وَالْآخَرُ يَنْهَاهُ عَنْهُ، كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ؟ فَقَالَ: يُرَجِّئُهُ حَتَّى يَلْقَى مَنْ يُخْبِرَهُ، فَهُوَ فِي سَعَةٍ حَتَّى يَلْقَاهُ

translations.en: I asked him about a man who was answered oppositely by two of his co-religionists regarding a matter which both transmit: one of them orders him to take it, while the other forbids him from it. What should he do? He said: He withholds [action] until he meets one who will inform him, and he is in ease/respite until he meets him.

chunks.arabic_text: وَفِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى: بِأَيِّهِمَا أَخَذْتَ مِنْ بَابِ التَّسْلِيمِ وَسِعَكَ

translations.en: And in another narration: Whichever of them you act upon, from the door of submission/compliance, suffices you.

en.summary: The Imam provides a legal ruling for a person who receives contradictory narrations from two reliable sources. He advises postponing action until a definitive answer is found, granting the person a period of ease. Alternatively, if one acts upon either narration with the intention of compliance (taslim), that action is sufficient.
en.seo_question: How to handle contradictory religious rulings from two sources?

key_terms.وَسِعَكَ: it suffices you/is easy for you
